questions.explain: Osmosis is the movement of water across a partially permeable membrane.

questions.prompt: A plant cell is placed in a concentrated salt solution. What happens?
options: Water enters and the cell bursts
Water leaves and the cell becomes plasmolysed
questions.explain: The outside is hypertonic, so water moves out and the cytoplasm pulls away from the wall.

questions.prompt: Why don’t plant cells burst in pure water?
options: The strong cell wall stops them over-expanding
questions.explain: The cell becomes turgid, pressing against the wall.

questions.prompt: A solution that has the same concentration as the inside of a cell is called…

feedback.1: Hypotonic means more dilute than the cell.

questions.prompt: A potato strip weighs 4.0 g before and 4.4 g after soaking. What is the percentage change in mass?
A strip of 5.0 g loses 20% of its mass in strong sugar solution. What is its new mass?
Potato strips gain mass in 0.1 mol/L and lose mass in 0.5 mol/L sugar solution. What can you conclude?
options: The potato cells’ concentration is between 0.1 and 0.5 mol/L
The potato cells are pure water
The cells are more concentrated than 0.5 mol/L
questions.explain: No change would occur at the concentration equal to the cells’.

questions.prompt: Explain why a doctor gives a patient 0.9% saline in a drip rather than pure water.
questions.modelAnswer: 0.9% saline is isotonic with blood, so there is no net movement of water into or out of red blood cells and they keep their shape. Pure water would be hypotonic: water would enter the red blood cells by osmosis and they could swell and burst, which is dangerous.
rubric: Red cells would swell and burst by osmosis
questions.explain: Criterion A/D: applying osmosis to medicine.
